key_insight: Combining structured EHR features, clinical-text embeddings, and knowledge-grounded entity extraction improved sensitivity for 30-day diabetic readmission prediction, but slightly reduced AUROC.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help identify more patients who are later readmitted, although low specificity may increase false-positive alerts.
method: Fuse engineered EHR features with 32 compressed Bio_ClinicalBERT embedding components.
Extract symbolic entities using hybrid retrieval, cross-encoder re-ranking, and reflective negation auditing.
Predict readmission with cost-sensitive XGBoost and a threshold calibrated using Youden’s J.
evidence_signal: Using a patient-grouped 80/20 split of 101,766 encounters, the model achieved sensitivity of 0.6667 versus 0.5839 and Brier score of 0.0977 versus 0.1080 on 20,153 held-out encounters; AUROC fell from 0.6477 to 0.6375.
watch_item: Prospective clinical utility remains unestablished; specificity of 0.5161 warrants careful assessment of false-positive burden before deployment.
paper_title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
